sources.title: Jewel Changi Airport
sources.locator: Singapore, 2019 project header and Waterfall feature
sources.supports: Safdie Architects describes the glass roof’s oculus, the Rain Vortex and indoor garden. The project record describes recirculated rainwater and collecting water for reuse.

sources.title: Jewel Rain Vortex
sources.supports: The operator identifies the installation as the Rain Vortex in the Forest Valley and describes places from which visitors can see it.

cards.title: Water through Jewel’s roof
cards.text: Safdie Architects’ 2019 Singapore project has a glass roof opening above the Rain Vortex. Water falls into the interior beside the Forest Valley garden. The architect describes recirculation and rainwater reuse.
cards.limits: The public view shows where water travels. A water balance and power reading would need measurements from the installation over a stated period.

exhibits.name: Jewel Rain Vortex, Singapore
exhibits.dateKind: The project record dates the building in Singapore. The year describes the project.
exhibits.summary: An opening in the glass roof sends water down beside the Forest Valley. Safdie Architects describes recirculated rainwater and rainwater reuse. The visitor attraction and circulation system have their own records.
exhibits.altText: Original diagram of an opening in a glass roof, a pale waterfall and planted banks inside Jewel.

items.name: The Archive’s punched setup strip
items.description: The strip records the display setting and a return route. Its readings belong to the Bell Archive inlet. Ivo can use these settings to begin a fresh test on the Island.

missions.title: The Water That Comes Back
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What can a visitor see about water use from the display alone?
missions.stake: The Bell Archive has one attendant. Its visitor model can hold a reserve for little gardens or run a powered tide plate.

objectives.title: Run two setups and clip the basin, return and spill readings for each.
Punch a checked setup on a strip for Ivo.

missions.title: A Smaller Inlet
missions.knowledgeQuestion: Which parts of a working setup can travel to a different site?
missions.stake: The Island’s old rain garden and powered tide plate share an attendant. Its inlet is smaller and its plate draws more power.

objectives.title: Fit a starting card and check all three gauges at the Island manifold.
Open one service, take its side path and read the destination.

hints.text: Find the Bell Archive’s model, beside the Jewel catalogue case.
Fit a short shower or long curtain, with a near or lifted return. Run two pulses.
Visit the three gauge stands around the model. Clip each reading before changing the model settings.
Run a second setup, then clip its three readings. Both entries appear under Completed gauge records.
The file needs a setup and the service it can support.
The lifted return adds to the reserve and spends power. The tide plate needs spare power at both pulses.
At the model, choose a service the latest measured setup can support.
Use Keep the rain garden path open or Power the public tide plate. The punched strip goes in your bag.
Ivo’s circulation model is in the Island’s Plan Workshop.
Fit the Bell Archive strip or Ivo’s local card. Both begin a test under the Island’s own conditions.
Run two pulses, then look for the basin staff, return counter and spill tray across the workshop.
Clip all three readings from the same run. Return to the model to see which service it supports.
One attendant can open one side path. The ordinary route to Quiet Margin stays in use.
The garden needs stored water. The tide plate needs spare power at both pulses.
A short shower and lifted return can hold the garden reserve. A near return can leave power for the plate.
Set the supported service on the model. Enter its workshop side gate, then read the display near your landing square.

journal.text: Some water passed the display more than once. The basin and spill tray kept separate counts. The Island used a fresh test because its inlet and power demands differed from the Archive’s.

chronicle.title: A path to the rain garden
chronicle.text: The attendant opened the closer garden path while the basin held enough for the next draw.

chronicle.title: A light above the covered path
chronicle.text: The covered passage opened when the tide plate had enough power across both pulses.
